texts: The villagers tell wraith stories at Lantern-night.
A favorite story concerns the bad winter of sixty-three years ago.
Four wraiths rose in succession sixty-three years ago.
In that winter three Keepers walked the Cove Stair together every evening.

fields.sentence: The villagers tell wraith stories at Lantern-night.

q1_issues.issue: "Lantern-night" carries its kind word inside the name, which *Names and casing* says is stated in one ordinary type atom beside the `Name` fact (its "the Kestrel River" example emits `(Member kestrel_river river)`), but no `(Member lantern_night night)` atom is emitted.

review.notes: Definite plural to group witness, plus the group event and the per-member distribution rule at (STV 1.0 0.9) for the distributive predicate, is right; so is the bare kind filler for the non-specific plural object and the `Time` head for the named time.

issues.reason: *Names and casing* requires the entity's kind in one ordinary type atom "whether the kind word sits inside the name or beside it" - its own "the Kestrel River" -> (Member kestrel_river river) example - and *Core patterns* names "a kind word inside the name itself" as a licensing source, so the missing (Member lantern_night night) leaves a named referent typed nowhere.

new_gaps: A NAMED TIME whose name carries its kind word ("Lantern-night", "Midsummer Eve") falls between two sections that do not meet: *Time* says a named time "stays a bare symbol" on Time and bars Member atoms for deictic times, while *Names and casing* mandates the type atom for a name carrying its kind word. The kind word here (night) is additionally a reserved day-part constant on Time, so the type atom overloads that symbol - a licensed form would need to state whether a Time-filler name is typed at all and, if so, which symbol carries the day-part sense.
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form adds (Member lantern_night night) (STV 1.0 0.99) beside the existing Name atom; the rest of the parse stands.
adjudication.notes: The rest is doctrinal: group witness for the definite plural, group event plus the per-member distribution rule for the distributive predicate, the bare kind filler for the non-specific plural object, the compound's head genus with the noun modifier unexposed, and no status atom on the habitual present.

fields.sentence: A favorite story concerns the bad winter of sixty-three years ago.

review.notes: Stative-transitive "concerns" correctly keeps Agent/Theme (stativity and inanimacy never demote a transitive subject), "favorite"/"bad" stay unfused descriptive atoms, and the event-noun winter takes (BeforeBy sk_winter_1 now 63 year) directly with no tense atom of its own, since no clause predicates its occurrence.

fields.sentence: Four wraiths rose in succession sixty-three years ago.

q2_gaps: Sequential-ordering adverbial "in succession" (the members of a counted plural act one after another, not simultaneously): the instruction set gives sequence/ordering adverbials no slot (Manner is barred, and it answers neither an aboutness question for the preposition-named oblique nor a period/rate question for Every/TimesPer), so the parse must drop it; there is also no carrier for the intra-group ordering it states, which the group event plus per-member rule leaves unexpressed.
review.notes: Dropping "in succession" is what the adverb rule directs, so it is a coverage gap rather than a defect. Counted-plural group + Cardinality + group event + per-member rule (status inside the consequent) all follow doctrine, and "sixty-three years ago" correctly anchors on the reserved `now` via BeforeBy.

fields.sentence: In that winter three Keepers walked the Cove Stair together every evening.

q1_issues.issue: 'that winter' is minted as an sk_ witness carrying a (Member sk_winter_1 winter) type atom, which the Time section forbids for a time expression.
(Time sk_walk_1 sk_winter_1) puts a witness symbol in the Time slot, whose licensed fillers are structured calendar terms or bare time constants.

q2_gaps: anaphoric temporal NP with no antecedent, at season granularity ('in that winter') - the term-propagation rule presupposes an antecedent event supplying calendar terms, and this item has none

past-tense habitual bounded in a past interval ('walked ... every evening') - the frequency rule says the recurring event stays unmarked while the finite-clause tense rule marks (Past e), and the instruction set does not say which wins
review.notes: 'together' is correctly consumed as the collective marker (group event, no per-member rule), and 'the Cove Stair' correctly gets one opaque name symbol plus a separate ordinary kind atom.

issues.reason: Time treats a time expression as a term or bare constant and forbids minting an sk_ witness or a Member atom for one — the sk_-entity contrast it draws is explicitly for event-denoting nouns ('the show', 'the storm'), and a season is a time span, not an eventuality — so (Member sk_winter_1 winter) types a time as an entity.

Time enumerates the role's fillers — structured calendar terms (Year/Month/Day/Weekday/Hour/Minute), day-part symbols, and deictic or named constants — and a minted witness is none of them, so (Time sk_walk_1 sk_winter_1) is ill-typed per the vocabulary and unreachable by the seeded calendar and ordering rules that consume Time terms.

gaps_confirmed: Anaphoric temporal NP with no antecedent, at season granularity ('in that winter'): term propagation presupposes an antecedent event supplying the calendar terms to copy, and the stated fallback ('emit just the day-part') is given only at day granularity, with no season term defined beside (Year/Month/Day/Weekday).

Past-tense habitual bounded in a past interval ('walked ... every evening'): the frequency rule leaves the recurring event unmarked while the finite-clause tense rule marks (Past e), and the instruction set does not say which wins.
adjudication.defect_summary: Compliant form: the bare season constant in the Time slot — (Time sk_walk_1 winter), the season analogue of the stated 'if the antecedent's day is unknown, emit just the day-part' fallback — with no sk_winter_1 witness and no (Member ... winter) atom.
adjudication.notes: The rest is right: 'together' is correctly consumed as the collective marker (one group event, no per-member rule), 'the Cove Stair' takes the Kestrel-River shape of one opaque name symbol plus a separate ordinary kind atom, and 'every evening' correctly yields the slot term plus (Every ... 1 day).
